content:
Two Pow ℤˣ ℕ instances are non defeq at reducible transparency:

module

public import Mathlib.Data.ZMod.IntUnitsPower

lemma test : Int.instUnitsPow (R := ℕ) = NPow.toPow := by
  with_reducible rfl -- fails

Do we really want docs#Int.instUnitsPow ??

/-- There is a canonical power operation on `ℤˣ` by `R` if `Additive ℤˣ` is an `R`-module.

In lemma names, this operation is called `uzpow` to match `zpow`.

Notably this is satisfied by `R ∈ {ℕ, ℤ, ZMod 2}`. -/
instance Int.instUnitsPow : Pow ℤˣ R where
  pow u r := (r • Additive.ofMul u).toMul

In this file #synth Pow ℤˣ X already works for X = {ℕ, ℤ} so two out of the three potential applications are unnecessary (and seem to be causing diamonds). How about we just remove this instance and replace it with Pow ℤˣ (ZMod 2) if that's what we actually want? [Module R (Additive ℤˣ)] seems like a very weird hypothesis in practice. The only reason it's true for ZMod 2 is that it's proved just above in the same file.

The file Mathlib.Data.ZMod.IntUnitsPower is only imported in Mathlib.Algebra.Ring.NegOnePow and Mathlib.LinearAlgebra.TensorProduct.Graded.External. In the first of these two files, the import can just be replaced by importing the the files which Mathlib.Data.ZMod.IntUnitsPower imports (presumably shake didn't spot this because it was using the second instance of Pow ℤˣ ℤ defined in the file). But the second of these files actually has an [Module ι (Additive ℤˣ)] hypothesis. Is there a less convoluted way of doing whatever is going on in this file? @Eric Wieser this looks like your doing.

I think [CommSemiring ι] [Module ι (Additive ℤˣ)] means something close to "ι is equipped with a ring homomorphism to ZMod 2" so one approach to unravelling all of this might be instead assuming [Algebra ι (ZMod 2)], making Pow ℤˣ (ZMod 2) and then just raising units to the power of algebraMap (ZMod 2) x instead of x.
have s : ℤˣ := ((-1 : ℤˣ) ^ (i.1 * i.2 : ι) : ℤˣ) in External.lean already shows that typeclass inference is having a hard time with this instance.

Kevin Buzzard said:

@Eric Wieser this looks like your doing.

Note that

lemma test : Int.instUnitsPow (R := ℕ) = NPow.toPow := by
  rfl -- succeeds

so this isn't necessarily a bad instance, just a bad implementation.
If Additive were a one-field structure then with_reducible rfl would pass, I believe

Kevin Buzzard said:

I think [CommSemiring ι] [Module ι (Additive ℤˣ)] means something close to "ι is equipped with a ring homomorphism to ZMod 2" so one approach to unravelling all of this might be instead assuming [Algebra ι (ZMod 2)], making Pow ℤˣ (ZMod 2) and then just raising units to the power of algebraMap (ZMod 2) x instead of x.

I think I avoided this because otherwise you end up with a bunch of annoying algebraMaps in the statement, and have to decide which of (-1 : ℤˣ) ^ algebraMap _ (ZMod 2) (i.1 * i.2) and (-1 : ℤˣ) ^ (algebraMap _ (ZMod 2) i.1 * algebraMap _ (ZMod 2) i.2) to use in lemmas (the first is shorter but the second is simp-normal)

Fixed in #41999. The issue was that the equality toAdd (ofAdd x) = x did not hold at implicit reducibility, so I added implicit_reducible on toAdd and ofAdd.

Note that the correct check for diamonds is not with_reducible but with_implicit: instance equality is checked at implicit reducibility. After the PR, the following works:

example : Int.instUnitsPow = NPow.toPow := by with_implicit rfl
